items.question: On a technically adequate view, the anatomy in one plane looks abnormal, but you cannot say what the lesion is. What next?
options: The fetus is a candidate for fetal echocardiography: a suspected abnormality is enough
Wait until you can name the lesion
Report the heart as normal if the four-chamber view is normal
Repeat the scan after delivery
items.explanation: Fetuses with a known or suspected abnormality on cardiac screening are candidates for fetal echocardiography.

items.question: The mother has pregestational diabetes with a good HbA1c. How does the guideline list this?
options: As an indication for fetal echocardiography, whatever the HbA1c
As an indication only if the HbA1c is raised
Among factors with insufficient evidence of raised risk
Among factors where echocardiography may be considered
items.explanation: Pregestational diabetes is listed as an indication regardless of HbA1c.

items.question: Gestational diabetes was diagnosed in the third trimester. How does the guideline class this factor?
options: Insufficient evidence that risk is significantly above baseline
A common indication, like all diabetes
A factor where echocardiography may be considered
Not mentioned in the guideline
items.explanation: Gestational diabetes diagnosed after the second trimester is among the factors with insufficient evidence of raised risk. Pregestational diabetes is different.

items.question: An isolated echogenic intracardiac focus is seen and the heart is otherwise normal on screening. What does the guideline say about risk?
options: Evidence is insufficient that risk of heart disease is significantly above baseline
It is a common indication for fetal echocardiography
It indicates a ventricular septal defect
It indicates an arrhythmia
items.explanation: Echogenic intracardiac focus is listed among factors with insufficient evidence of risk significantly above baseline.

items.question: The fetus's older sibling had surgery for congenital heart disease. How does the guideline list this?
options: As an indication: congenital heart disease in a first-degree relative of the fetus
Not listed: only parents count as first-degree relatives
Among factors where echocardiography may be considered
Among factors with insufficient evidence of raised risk
items.explanation: Congenital heart disease in a first-degree relative of the fetus (parents, siblings and half-siblings) is a listed indication. A second-degree relative falls under 'may be considered'.

items.question: The pregnancy was conceived by IVF with ICSI. What does the guideline say?
options: Fetal echocardiography may be considered
Fetal echocardiography is a firm indication
Evidence is insufficient that risk is raised
The routine cardiac screen can be omitted
items.explanation: Conception by IVF, including ICSI, is in the group where fetal echocardiography may be considered.

items.question: Which of these is a listed fetal indication for fetal echocardiography?
options: Hydrops
Isolated single umbilical artery
A non-cardiac soft marker
Abnormal serum analytes
items.explanation: Hydrops is a listed fetal indication. The other three are among factors with insufficient evidence of raised risk.

items.question: The mother takes paroxetine. Another mother takes a different SSRI. How does the guideline treat them?
options: Paroxetine: echocardiography may be considered. Other SSRIs: insufficient evidence of raised risk
Both are firm indications
Neither is mentioned
Other SSRIs are an indication; paroxetine is not
items.explanation: Paroxetine is named among selected teratogens where echocardiography may be considered. SSRI exposure other than paroxetine is in the insufficient-evidence group.

items.question: The mother is known to have anti-Ro/SSA antibodies. How does the guideline list this?
options: As an indication for fetal echocardiography
As an indication only once the fetal heart rate is slow
Among factors with insufficient evidence of raised risk
It is not mentioned
items.explanation: Anti-Ro/SSA antibodies are among the listed maternal indications.

items.question: At 20 weeks the left ventricle is clearly smaller than the right. What is the correct reading?
options: It warrants further examination; causes include coarctation and an evolving hypoplastic left heart
A normal variant at this gestation
Normal if the heart rate is regular
Recheck only in the third trimester
items.explanation: Mild disproportion can be a variant in the third trimester, but right-left asymmetry in mid-gestation warrants further examination.

items.question: Who is best placed to perform the fetal echocardiogram?
options: A trained specialist familiar with prenatal diagnosis and with postnatal course, management and prognosis
Any sonologist with a machine that has colour Doppler
A general paediatrician after delivery
Whoever made the referral, with or without specialist training
items.explanation: Fetal echocardiography is best performed by a trained specialist familiar with prenatal diagnosis, postnatal course, postnatal management and prognosis.

items.question: Which observation explains why quality routine screening of every pregnancy matters?
options: A high proportion of prenatally detectable heart disease occurs in pregnancies with no risk factor
Risk factors are rarely recorded correctly
Fetal echocardiography is unreliable when a risk factor is present
Heart disease cannot be detected before birth unless a risk factor is present
items.explanation: A high proportion of prenatally detectable heart disease occurs in pregnancies with no risk factor or extracardiac anomaly, so quality screening and timely referral matter.
